description: Check this machine's requirements (runtime, RAM, ports); install nothing.
Show what is installed, whether each component is healthy, and which datasets are loaded. Exit codes: 0 running, 3 database stopped, 4 not installed. --json prints one machine-readable object.
Show kit source, install date, and component versions.
Compare installed versions against the versions the maintainers advertise, and print the exact update command for each.

Apply the advertised versions of the quick components (kit, exapump, MCP server, pyexasol, installed add-ons); a runtime change is announced but left for you to run explicitly. Database data is preserved.
Handle Exasol Personal major-version updates with an explicit non-destructive plan, deployment backup, and launcher apply step.
Add the Kit 2 trust assets (Trusted AI Workflow add-on) on top of this install: semantic model, audit/run log, saved workflow. Nothing is reinstalled and no data is touched; safe to re-run.
Remove exactly what upgrade-kit2 added and return to Kit 1. The database, exapump, MCP server and sample data stay untouched.
Re-stage the Kit 2 assets from the current kit copy (valid once Kit 2 is installed). A newer asset bundle arrives with the kit itself.

Print the connection details panel (DSN, users, schema). --json prints the install record (~/.exasol-starter-kit/manifest.json) verbatim on stdout, with nothing else on it, so scripts and support threads can read it.
Friendly walkthrough: connect AI clients (MCP), SQL clients (DBeaver or DbVisualizer), and Python (pyexasol).
Start everything the kit runs: the local Exasol database (deploying or starting it as needed) and every installed add-on service.
Stop the add-on services and the local Exasol database.

Rebuild a database that cannot be started (the launcher reports it interrupted and every start fails the same way). DESTRUCTIVE: the deployment is replaced and its data is not recoverable; bundled datasets are reloaded afterwards. --yes (or EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_REPAIR=1) pre-answers the confirmation.

Whether the database and add-on services come back automatically after a restart (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux, the container restart policy for Nano). No argument shows the current state.

Open the focused data-loading menu: bundled sample data or a local CSV/Parquet/JSON file (JSON is shredded into tables by the JSON Tables add-on, offered on the spot). --force reloads instead of skipping what is already there. Non-interactively, EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather names exactly which bundled datasets to load, and it composes with --force.

Run one SQL statement against the local database and translate a failure into the remedy (connection refused -> exakit start; FETCH FIRST/TOP -> LIMIT; object not found -> describe it first). Reads only unless --write. It connects with the starter-kit profile, which is the ADMIN user and is NOT sandboxed - the read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command.
Permanently configure MCP in supported AI clients.
Show managed MCP state for all supported AI clients.
Validate managed MCP configs and test connectivity.

Check the configured MCP clients and repair what has drifted, then re-check. Checks the database is running first (exit 3 + 'exakit start' when it is not). --json reports the diagnosis without repairing.
Remove the managed MCP config from the supported clients.
Restore the latest (or a chosen) MCP config snapshot.
List the AI skills this kit carries — one per component and add-on — with a one-line summary and whether each has reached the agents' discovery folders. --json prints one machine-readable object.
Install the kit's AI skills into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills for CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex).

Browse optional add-ons (dash-server, Exasol for VS Code, JSON Tables): Space selects, Enter installs. Installed add-ons update through exakit update; tools you installed yourself are recognised and never re-offered.

Pick what to remove (Skip, each add-on, or EVERYTHING) with a confirmation summary and a typed gate; single components by name (exakit uninstall mcp_configs). --dry-run previews the full plan; --yes is the scripted full uninstall.

Every log the kit can show: the installer run, the database container, each add-on service, and what the boot entries wrote at login. No target lists them with size and last-updated; -f follows one live; --path prints its path. --json lists the targets (with each one's path, size and last-updated) as one machine-readable object.

Browse or search every exakit, exapump, and exasol command (this screen). --json prints the whole command surface as one machine-readable object (tool, command, options, description), so an agent can discover what the CLI can do without parsing the decorated screen.
Show the exakit usage text (--all: every command). Any subcommand also answers --help with its catalog entry.
Run a single SQL statement through a saved connection profile.
Run a SQL script file (via stdin) through a profile.
Bulk-load a CSV or Parquet file into a table.
Create or update a named connection profile (host, port, user, password).
Print the exapump version.
Show exapump's built-in help.
Override the config path; profiles live in ~/.exapump/config.toml. Kit default profile: starter-kit.
Read-only MCP server the AI client runs to query Exasol over stdio.
Run the Exasol MCP server in HTTP mode instead of stdio.
Kit provisions a least-privilege mcp_readonly user with database-wide read and no write (DSN default 127.0.0.1:8563).
